acceptance.criterion_verbatim: S20-AC1 -- THE CENSUS HAS ALL THREE DENOMINATORS AND NAMES ITS SOURCES: firms observed of firms expected (with the expected set derived from a live read of the partner tables, not recalled); addresses per firm; the window start and end. Each observation attributed to the log source it came from, with a statement of what each source cannot see.
acceptance.invocation: aws dynamodb list-tables for the expected firm set; aws logs describe-log-groups + describe-log-streams for the two WAF sources; aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers + describe-load-balancer-attributes and aws s3api list-objects-v2 for the ALB source; CloudWatch Logs Insights over aws-waf-logs-opal-cloudfront for the population, the exact-path census, the User-Agent census and the 30-minute time bins
acceptance.output_evidence: DENOMINATOR 1, FIRMS OBSERVED OF FIRMS EXPECTED = 0 of 4. Expected set read LIVE, not recalled: list-tables returns 38 tables with LastEvaluatedTableName ABSENT (so 38 is a true denominator, not a page), of which 4 match opal-partner-*: 49financial, cottonwood, demo, inflection. DENOMINATOR 2, ADDRESSES PER FIRM = 0 for all four, and the reason is structural rather than sparse -- see S20-AC2. DENOMINATOR 3, THE WINDOWS, PER SOURCE: aws-waf-logs-opal-cloudfront 2026-09-03T10:20:36Z to 2026-09-04T01:24:12Z (15.06h, 2,771 records, recordsScanned 2771 = recordsMatched 2771); aws-waf-logs-opal-gateway 2026-08-15T02:56:15Z to 2026-09-04T00:56:32Z (~19.7d); ALB opal-gateway access logs at s3://opal-data-security/waf-logs/alb-opal-gateway 2026-09-03T09:43:36Z to 2026-09-04T01:35:05Z (15.9h, 166 objects, 532,775 bytes, IsTruncated absent). SOURCE ATTRIBUTION AND WHAT EACH CANNOT SEE: (a) aws-waf-logs-opal-cloudfront fronts the PORTAL and is the ONLY source that observes /auth/login at all -- 695 exact-path events; it cannot see request bodies, so it cannot see which firm signed in. (b) aws-waf-logs-opal-gateway fronts the gateway, a JSON-RPC/OAuth surface; it yielded 2 exact-path /auth/login events over 19.7 days (figure RELAYED from 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~S Msg-ID 20084 and NOT re-measured here, because re-running that seat's query would be repetition rather than corroboration); it cannot see portal sign-ins because they do not traverse it. (c) The ALB source is the SAME SURFACE as (b) -- describe-load-balancers returns exactly 1 load balancer, opal-gateway, so there is no portal ALB; it cannot see portal sign-ins for the same reason, and it records connection-level access rather than firm identity.
acceptance.denominator: Firms: 0 observed of 4 expected (from 38 tables scanned). Addresses per firm: 0 for each of the 4. Windows: 15.06h / 19.7d / 15.9h across the three named sources. Exact-path sign-in population: 695 of 2,771 records on the only source that sees it.
acceptance.status_reason: All three denominators are present and each observation is attributed to the source it came from, including an explicit statement of what each source structurally cannot see. The gateway figure is labelled RELAYED rather than presented as this seat's own measurement -- a relayed number that loses its qualifier is how a census silently acquires evidence it never took.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: S20-AC2 -- ZERO-ADDRESS FIRMS ARE LISTED, NOT OMITTED: every expected firm with no observed address named explicitly, each labelled "did not sign in during the window" or "log coverage unknown for this path". A census that silently drops them is a FAIL -- those are exactly the firms C-4 exists to protect.
acceptance.invocation: The four expected firms enumerated from the live list-tables read, then each checked against the exact-path census output and against the field inventory of a sampled /auth/login record
acceptance.output_evidence: ALL FOUR EXPECTED FIRMS ARE ZERO-ADDRESS AND ARE NAMED HERE RATHER THAN OMITTED: opal-partner-49financial -- LOG COVERAGE UNKNOWN FOR THIS PATH. opal-partner-cottonwood -- LOG COVERAGE UNKNOWN FOR THIS PATH. opal-partner-demo -- LOG COVERAGE UNKNOWN FOR THIS PATH. opal-partner-inflection -- LOG COVERAGE UNKNOWN FOR THIS PATH. EVERY ONE TAKES THE 'log coverage unknown' LABEL AND NOT 'did not sign in during the window', AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE CRITERION: no field on any of the three sources maps an address to a firm, so these four would have read as zero-address EVEN IF ALL FOUR HAD SIGNED IN REPEATEDLY DURING THE WINDOW. Proven on the record rather than argued: a sampled /auth/login record is httpMethod POST with args '' and the complete header set Accept-Encoding, Content-Length, Host, User-Agent, Content-Type, Connection -- no Cookie and no tenant-bearing field; the firm-identifying credential travels in the JSON body (Content-Length 84, Content-Type application/json) and WAF does not log bodies. Claiming 'did not sign in' for any of these four would assert a fact this census has no instrument to establish.
acceptance.denominator: 4 of 4 expected firms are zero-address; 4 of 4 labelled 'log coverage unknown for this path'; 0 labelled 'did not sign in during the window'.
acceptance.status_reason: This is the criterion the face names as the control that must be able to fail, and it fired. A census that returned a clean list with no zero-address firms would have meant the seat had not looked; this one returns the maximum possible number of them, 4 of 4, and assigns each the label the evidence actually supports rather than the label that would look tidier.

mutant.description: The face names the control that must be able to fail: S20-AC2 -- 'a census that produces a clean list with no zero-address firms named has probably not looked for them.' The mutant is a census that reports only the firms it happened to observe and silently drops the rest, which reads as a clean, confident result and is exactly the shape that would arm BLOCK against an unobserved partner office.
mutant.expected: If the control is real, the census must be able to RETURN zero-address firms and must distinguish the two reasons for a zero -- 'did not sign in during the window' versus 'log coverage unknown for this path' -- rather than collapsing them into one silent absence.
mutant.observed: It returned the maximum possible number of zero-address firms, 4 of 4, and assigned every one of them the 'log coverage unknown for this path' label rather than the tidier 'did not sign in'. The distinction was forced by evidence rather than asserted: a sampled /auth/login record carries no Cookie and no tenant-bearing field and the firm-identifying credential is in an unlogged JSON body, so all four would have read zero-address even had they signed in continuously. A census that had reported 'did not sign in during the window' for these four would have passed this criterion while asserting a fact it had no instrument to establish.

determinism.method: The load-bearing figure -- that the window's sign-in traffic is dominated by this project's own instrumentation -- was established on TWO INDEPENDENT AXES rather than by repeating one query: a User-Agent census over the 695 exact-path events, and a 30-minute time-bin distribution over the same population. The two share no field. The exact-path census and the total-population count were each run against the same window with service-printed recordsScanned/recordsMatched statistics.
determinism.expected: If the contamination finding is real rather than an artifact of one filter, the two axes must agree closely on the contaminated fraction despite sharing no field.
determinism.observed: They agree to within one tenth of a percentage point: the User-Agent axis gives 680 of 695 = 97.8%, and the time-bin axis gives 679 of 695 = 97.7%. The exact-path census returned the same 695 matched against a 2,771 population on repeat invocation.
